D1 research authoring, batch 81 (2026-09-27): three ASSOCIATION_ONLY draft mappings added at ranks 1, 2, and 3 (diabetes-mellitus, multiple-myeloma, interstitial-lung-disease) pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; mapping approval is not citation verification. All three edges draw on the same 44-patient multicentre series, which is the only located source reporting more than one of the three classical scleredema associates in a single cohort, and the three edges are therefore registered as PARALLEL rather than as a chain, since no edge in this file is presented as producing another.

Classification guard: all three edges assert association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true), at MULTIFACTORIAL for the diabetes and myeloma routes and at MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE for the pulmonary route. The multicentre series' explicit NULL for a preceding respiratory tract infection is registered openly on the diabetes edge rather than omitted, because it contradicts the classical post-streptococcal teaching and changes what a reviewer should look for. The myeloma edge records BOTH the paraprotein-as-agent and paraprotein-as-marker readings without choosing between them, and frames the edge as a screening proposition requiring electrophoresis, immunofixation, free light chains, and marrow assessment. The pulmonary edge discloses on its face that the located evidence describes a chest-wall mechanical RESTRICTIVE PATTERN while the catalog identity denotes a PARENCHYMAL process, and requires the reviewing clinician to distinguish the two before the target is treated as met.

Withheld routes and duplicate-scope screen: NO scleroderma edge (DIFFERENTIAL, DISCLOSED - this is the most consequential withholding in the batch and it is recorded rather than authored, because scleredema and scleroderma are typically MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE diagnoses that are confused with one another rather than co-occurring: the located mimic case explicitly reports a patient who did NOT meet American College of Rheumatology or EULAR systemic sclerosis criteria, had no Raynaud's phenomenon, negative systemic sclerosis autoantibodies, and normal nail fold capillaroscopy, so the located evidence argues AGAINST co-occurrence rather than for it, and authoring an association edge would assert the opposite of what the source says); no infection or post-streptococcal edge (NULL - the largest located series reports that a preceding respiratory tract infection was not a feature, so the classical third associate has no support in the located evidence and is recorded as a documented null rather than authored); no thyroid or hypothyroidism edge (the endocrine associations in the largest series are reported jointly as endocrine and metabolic disease without thyroid-specific figures, so no thyroid-specific edge is supportable from these anchors); and no cachexia, obesity, or metabolic-syndrome edge (MISSING IDENTITY - metabolic syndrome and obesity are named in the located conclusions but have no catalog identity).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The diabetes association in scleredema is the largest and best-replicated of its three classical associates, and the located evidence includes both a multicentre series and a prospective screening study in a diabetes population: a multicentre retrospective study of 44 patients with scleredema reports that the most common associated disorders were endocrine and metabolic diseases, with 30 of the 44 patients suffering from diabetes, mostly type 2, concludes that scleredema is a chronic debilitating disease associated with diabetes and metabolic syndrome, and recommends that treatment of the primary disease including strict glycaemic control combined with physical therapy be employed (PMID 26304054); a prospective screening study of 113 consecutive patients with diabetes identified 11 new scleroedema adultorum of Buschke patients, a 9.7 percent prevalence, ALL of whom had type 2 diabetes, and characterised the newly identified cases with a focus on lipid metabolism abnormalities and vascular complications (PMID 33952255); and a case report of scleredema diabeticorum in a patient with poorly controlled diabetes documents extensive trunk involvement in a cuirasse pattern with associated restrictive lung disease, cutaneous ultrasonographic dermal thickening, and the observation that cutaneous hardness secondary to scleredema may cause limited mobility with respiratory manifestations assessable mainly where extensive scleredema involves trunk and shoulders (PMID 33865279); recorded as documented association only, with the direction carried as unresolved and the classic post-infectious teaching explicitly nulled.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of diabetes mellitus is established for any individual, and in this edge the direction is genuinely bidirectional and unresolvable from the located evidence: the multicentre series reports diabetes as a comorbidity OF scleredema in 30 of 44 patients, while the screening study reports scleredema as a newly identified condition IN a diabetes population, and neither design establishes which came first, so the honest reading is co-occurrence enriched in both directions rather than a route. The shared driver is plausibly upstream of both, since both conditions are associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and hyperinsulinaemia, and the screening study's own focus on dyslipidaemia and vascular complications indicates that the metabolic phenotype surrounds both diagnoses; the classic teaching that scleredema follows streptococcal or other infection is directly CONTRADICTED by the largest located series, which explicitly reports that a preceding respiratory tract infection was NOT a feature in its 44 patients, and that null is carried openly in the evidence gaps rather than omitted, because it changes what a reviewer should look for; the 9.7 percent screening prevalence is from a single tertiary centre in consecutively screened diabetes patients and may not generalise; and the case report is a single patient. Individual claims require a dated type 2 diabetes diagnosis with glycaemic control data and a dated scleredema diagnosis with distribution documented, plus exclusion of monoclonal gammopathy and of preceding streptococcal infection as alternative associates.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a shared metabolic and microvascular mechanism rather than a single causal agent: chronic hyperglycaemia and hyperinsulinaemia are proposed to drive non-enzymatic glycosylation of dermal collagen, which cross-links and stiffens collagen bundles, with the resulting thickened but non-indurated dermis of scleredema accumulating in the posterior neck and upper back where the mechanical loading and reduced mobility of the shoulders and upper back concentrate the abnormal connective tissue; the case report's observation that cutaneous hardness causes limited mobility with respiratory manifestations in extensive disease is offered as the located support for the mechanical-mobility component of the vector, while the overall multifactorial designation reflects that the located evidence cannot apportion between glycaemic drive, glycaemic duration, adiposity, and post-infectious triggers.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at multicentre-retrospective, prospective-screening, and case-report class, following the file's existing hormonal, metabolic, and treatment-related pathway scope: the multicentre series is the anchor that supplies the effect magnitude, 30 of 44 patients with diabetes mostly type 2, and it is registered together with its own null for preceding respiratory tract infection rather than with the comorbidity count alone, because that null is the finding that changes the differential (PMID 26304054); the screening study is the only located design that samples from the diabetes population rather than the scleredema population and is therefore the anchor that makes the association bidirectional in the data rather than merely in principle, and its all-type-2 finding is carried explicitly (PMID 33952255); and the case report supplies the restrictive-pulmonary and mobility observations that connect extensive disease to a functional consequence and are separately registered at this file's rank 3 edge (PMID 33865279). Because the direction is unresolvable and the upstream driver is plausibly shared, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, classifies it MULTIFACTORIAL rather than METABOLIC_OR_NUTRITIONAL to avoid implying a single established metabolic route, and routes individual attribution through paired dated diagnoses with glycaemic data.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The largest anchor is a 44-patient multicentre retrospective series with a mean age at diagnosis of 53.8 years and 26 men, so it is a small, demographically narrow, non-replicated sample and its 30-of-44 diabetes figure carries no confidence interval; the screening study is single-centre and reports 11 cases identified among 113 consecutively screened diabetes patients, so its 9.7 percent prevalence is an estimate from one institution's diabetes population and may be inflated by referral bias toward complex patients; the case report is a single patient with poorly controlled diabetes and a restrictive lung pattern, so it cannot establish frequency of either the subcutaneous pattern or the pulmonary complication; NO located anchor establishes temporal order in either direction, and none includes a diabetes-free comparison group for the scleredema outcome; the two located designs sample from opposite populations, so their figures are not directly comparable and no located anchor reports both prevalences from the same cohort; and the multicentre series explicitly reports that a preceding respiratory tract infection was not a feature, which is a null against the classical post-streptococcal teaching and is registered here so that a reviewer does not default to the infection-first history. The multiple-myeloma route was authored separately at rank 2 because the same multicentre series reports 5 confirmed monoclonal gammopathies in the same 44 patients, and the two edges are deliberately registered as parallel rather than as a chain.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The plasma-cell dyscrasia association is the most clinically consequential of the three classical scleredema associates, because it is the one in which the skin disease can be the presenting sign of an underlying malignancy, and the located evidence establishes this across a multicentre series, a treatment-response case report, and a documented progression case: a multicentre retrospective study of 44 patients with scleredema reports monoclonal gammopathies confirmed in 5 cases and that systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressive drugs were reserved for patients with severe disease in whom phototherapy had failed or FOR PATIENTS WITH MULTIPLE MYELOMA, with 2 of the 44 patients dying of cardiovascular complications due to myeloma and severe diabetes (PMID 26304054); a case report of monoclonal gammopathy-associated scleredema adultorum of Buschke in a patient with diabetes mellitus treated successfully with intravenous immunoglobulin and narrow-band ultraviolet B phototherapy documents the dyscrasia-skin pairing as a treatable entity (PMID 34858014); and a case report of scleredema in the setting of monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance with progression to multiple myeloma documents the dyscrasia evolving to frank myeloma with new-onset Raynaud phenomenon, splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and the development of a plasmacytoma (PMID 37701163); recorded as documented association only, with the explicit clinical reading that the skin disease signals a plasma-cell disorder requiring screening rather than causing one.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of multiple myeloma is established for any individual, and the located evidence actually runs against a causal reading of the skin-to-marrow direction: the multicentre series reports monoclonal gammopathy as a comorbidity identified in patients already carrying the skin diagnosis, with the myeloma deaths recorded as deaths FROM a malignancy these patients independently had, and the progression case documents the haematological course moving from monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance to myeloma with the skin disease as a co-traveler rather than as an agent, so the honest reading is that scleredema is a marker that can accompany or precede a plasma-cell dyscrasia. The alternative and partly competing reading is real and is carried openly: monoclonal immunoglobulin itself is proposed in the located literature as contributing to dermal mucin deposition, which would make the paraprotein a contributor rather than a bystander, and the located case report of paraproteinemia-associated scleredema responding to thalidomide is consistent with a paraprotein-mediated mechanism, but no located anchor in this edge tests that mechanism and it is recorded as an alternative rather than adopted. The 5-of-44 figure carries no confidence interval, and no located anchor reports a myeloma-free comparison group for the scleredema outcome. Individual claims require serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation, serum free light chains, and a documented bone marrow assessment, since the entire screening proposition is unimplementable without them.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a paraprotein-mediated contribution to dermal mucin deposition, in which clonal immunoglobulin produced by a plasma-cell clone is proposed to drive the fibroblast response and excessive dermal mucin accumulation that defines scleredema, with the alternative and simpler reading being that both the skin disease and the plasma-cell dyscrasia arise from a shared underlying state and that the paraprotein is a marker rather than an agent; the mechanism is classified MULTIFACTORIAL because the located evidence cannot choose between the paraprotein-as-agent and paraprotein-as-marker readings, and the clinical consequence is the same under either: a patient carrying scleredema warrants plasma-cell screening, and a patient carrying an established plasma-cell dyscrasia warrants a skin examination.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at multicentre-retrospective and case-report class alongside the file's rank 1 diabetes edge, and deliberately registered as a PARALLEL rather than a CHAIN: the same 44-patient multicentre series supplies both edges, reporting 30 patients with diabetes and 5 confirmed monoclonal gammopathies in the same cohort, so neither condition is presented as producing the other or as sitting between them. The multicentre series is the anchor that supplies both the frequency and the management implication, since it reports that systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressive drugs were reserved for severe patients in whom phototherapy had failed or who had multiple myeloma (PMID 26304054); the gammopathy case report establishes the dyscrasia-skin pairing as a distinct treatable entity with a documented response to intravenous immunoglobulin and narrow-band phototherapy (PMID 34858014); and the progression case documents monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance progressing to myeloma with a plasmacytoma, which is the located basis for treating the skin finding as a marker that can precede rather than merely accompany the haematological disease (PMID 37701163). Because the paraprotein may be agent or marker, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, records both readings explicitly, and makes the screening workup the operational requirement rather than any causal claim.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The frequency anchor is a 44-patient multicentre retrospective series reporting 5 confirmed monoclonal gammopathies, a small number from which no proportion should be quoted as a rate; two of the 44 patients died of cardiovascular complications attributed to myeloma and severe diabetes, which is 2 deaths in a cohort of 44 followed for a mean of 32.2 months and establishes that the association can be lethal without establishing any individual prognosis; the remaining 39 were alive, 30 with and 9 without skin disease, which is reported here because it shows the skin disease is neither necessary nor sufficient for survival in this cohort; BOTH case reports are single patients, one of which is a treatment-response report whose design cannot attribute the response to the regimen rather than to the underlying dyscrasia going into remission; no located anchor in this edge uses a comparator group; no located anchor reports how many patients with monoclonal gammopathy were screened for scleredema, so the reverse direction is entirely unmeasured; and the paraprotein-as-agent reading is supported only by case-level treatment response and is recorded as an alternative rather than adopted. The interstitial-lung-disease route was authored separately at rank 3 because the same case report documents restrictive pulmonary disease, and the scleroderma route was withheld as DIFFERENTIAL rather than association, as recorded in the file todo.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance or smoldering myeloma rather than established multiple myeloma, which the located progression case documents as a distinct preceding state
Shared underlying state in which the paraprotein is a marker of a plasma-cell clone rather than an agent of the skin disease
Diabetes-associated scleredema as the alternative associate, coexistent in the located case reports and requiring separation
Other causes of dermatomyositis-like or scleroderma-like skin thickening requiring biopsy and serology to separate

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Extensive scleredema is reported to carry a restrictive pulmonary consequence, and the located evidence documents both the functional pattern and the proposed route: a case report of scleredema diabeticorum in a patient with poorly controlled diabetes describes extensive scleredema adultorum of the trunk in a cuirasse pattern associated with restrictive lung disease, with cutaneous ultrasonography revealing marked thickening of the dermis and multiple echogenic spots, and states explicitly that cutaneous hardness secondary to scleredema may cause limited mobility, that respiratory manifestations may therefore be associated and assessed mainly in cases of extensive scleredema involving trunk and shoulders, and that cutaneous ultrasonography may be useful to monitor disease evolution and confirm the diagnosis (PMID 33865279); the multicentre series of 44 patients reports that phototherapy was the treatment associated with higher although partial response, that systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressive drugs were reserved for severe disease, and that two patients died of cardiovascular complications due to myeloma and severe diabetes, describing scleredema as a chronic debilitating disease (PMID 26304054); and a separate scleroderma-mimic case describes a patient with diffuse skin thickening of face, neck, arms, forearms, thighs, chest, and back, sparing the hands and feet, with associated arthralgia, dysphagia, and dyspnoea on exertion, a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing, and interstitial lung fibrosis on high-resolution computed tomography, diagnosed on biopsy as scleredema rather than systemic sclerosis (PMID 30088450); recorded as documented association only, with the route named as hypothesized and the entity-identity problem carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of an interstitial lung disease is established for any individual, and the strongest located support is a single case: the route described is a chest-wall and shoulder-girdle mechanical restriction from cutaneous hardness limiting chest-wall excursion, NOT an intrinsic parenchymal lung disease, and the located abstract for that case explicitly frames the respiratory manifestations as mechanical and as assessable mainly where extensive disease involves the trunk and shoulders. That distinction is material, because the catalog's interstitial-lung-disease identity denotes a parenchymal process with its own established routes, and a restrictive pattern produced by chest-wall induration is a different entity with a different treatment and a different evidentiary standard. The third anchor is more troubling for this edge: its patient had interstitial lung fibrosis on high-resolution computed tomography AND a restrictive pulmonary pattern, but that patient was diagnosed with scleredema as a scleroderma mimic and had MYELOMA, so the fibrosis in that case may be attributable to the underlying plasma-cell dyscrasia, to the excluded systemic sclerosis differential, or to scleredema, and the located abstract cannot apportion. Individual claims require pulmonary function testing with diffusion capacity, high-resolution computed tomography, exclusion of an underlying plasma-cell dyscrasia, and a documented distinction between chest-wall mechanical restriction and intrinsic parenchymal disease.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a mechanical chest-wall restriction: extensive scleredema involving the trunk, back, and shoulder girdle deposits mucin and glycosylated collagen in the reticular dermis, hardening the skin and subcutaneous fascia over the thorax and limiting chest-wall excursion, which reduces the tidal volumes available to a mechanically stiffened chest and produces a restrictive spirometric pattern; the vector is named as hypothesized and is offered explicitly as an alternative to the parenchymal route, because the located evidence supports a restrictive PATTERN without establishing that any parenchymal lung process underlies it, and the competing parenchymal explanation involving the paraprotein or an excluded connective-tissue disease is carried in the alternatives.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-report and multicentre-retrospective class, and at the weakest strength of the three edges in this file, which the conservative standard records explicitly rather than smoothing over: the primary anchor is a single case report of a restrictive pattern attributed to cutaneous hardness, the multicentre series supplies disease-severity and treatment context but reports NO pulmonary outcomes, and the third anchor supplies parenchymal fibrosis in a patient whose lung findings are confounded by myeloma and by the excluded systemic sclerosis differential. The case report is the anchor that supplies the explicit mechanical statement that cutaneous hardness may cause limited mobility with respiratory manifestations mainly in extensive disease (PMID 33865279); the multicentre series is registered for the chronic-debility and treatment-resistance context and is explicit in the evidence gaps that it reports no pulmonary outcome data (PMID 26304054); and the scleroderma-mimic case is registered for the parenchymal-fibrosis observation with its full confounding disclosed, so that a reviewer sees the countervailing evidence rather than a clean association (PMID 30088450). Because the located pattern is restrictive without established parenchymal disease, the conservative standard requires the reviewing clinician to distinguish chest-wall restriction from intrinsic parenchymal disease before the target identity is treated as met.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The primary anchor is ONE case report; the multicentre anchor of 44 patients reports no pulmonary function, imaging, or respiratory outcomes whatsoever, so it contributes severity context only and cannot be cited for a lung association; the third anchor is ONE case whose interstitial lung fibrosis is confounded by a confirmed underlying myeloma and by the fact that systemic sclerosis was the leading differential being excluded, so it is registered as countervailing rather than supporting evidence and its fibrosis cannot be attributed to scleredema; no located anchor reports a prevalence of restrictive physiology, pulmonary function abnormalities, or radiographic lung change in any scleredema cohort; no located anchor distinguishes chest-wall mechanical restriction from intrinsic parenchymal disease, which is the single question that determines whether the target identity is even the right one; no located anchor reports body-surface-area or extent-of-involvement as a predictor of pulmonary involvement; and there is a target-identity mismatch on the face of this edge, in that the catalog's interstitial-lung-disease denotes a parenchymal process whereas the located evidence describes a chest-wall mechanical pattern, and that mismatch is disclosed in the evidence gaps rather than papered over. The scleroderma route was reviewed and withheld as DIFFERENTIAL rather than association and is recorded in the file todo.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Chest-wall mechanical restriction from extensive cutaneous and subcutaneous induration, which produces a restrictive PATTERN without intrinsic parenchymal disease and may be the entire explanation in the located case
Pulmonary amyloid or other parenchymal involvement from the underlying monoclonal gammopathy or plasma-cell dyscrasia documented at this file's rank 2 edge
Interstitial lung disease from a coexisting connective-tissue disease, particularly systemic sclerosis, which the located literature identifies as the principal differential
Aspiration or infection-related lung disease, and cardiac or renal comorbidity contributing to dyspnoea

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because extensive scleredema involving the trunk and shoulder girdle is documented to carry a restrictive pulmonary consequence and because the target identity had seven registered incoming edges, none of them dermatological, so the cutaneous-to-pulmonary route was unrepresented. The conservative framing names the mechanical chest-wall vector as hypothesized, registers the parenchymal-fibrosis case as countervailing evidence with its myeloma and systemic-sclerosis confounding disclosed, states plainly that the multicentre series reports no pulmonary outcomes, and discloses the parenchymal-versus-mechanical target-identity mismatch on the face of the edge rather than resolving it silently.

sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Dermatol Online J. 2021;27(3):13030/qt71g4k3qf. Case report; abstract describes increased mucin deposition in the reticular dermis, three recognized variants with scleredema diabeticorum associated with diabetes mellitus, and states that cutaneous hardness secondary to scleredema may cause limited mobility and that respiratory manifestations may be associated and assessed mainly in cases of extensive scleredema involving trunk and shoulders.

sourceReferences.citation: Rongioletti F, Kaiser F, Cinotti E, et al. Scleredema. A multicentre study of characteristics, comorbidities, course and therapy in 44 patients J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2015 Dec;29(12):2399-404. doi: 10.1111/jdv.13272. PMID 26304054.
sourceReferences.note: Multicentre retrospective study of 44 patients with scleredema describing the disease as chronic and debilitating, reporting that treatments with different combination or sequential modalities were used with variable results, that phototherapy was associated with higher although partial response, and that 2 patients died of cardiovascular complications due to myeloma and severe diabetes; registered for disease-severity and treatment-resistance context only, as it reports no pulmonary outcomes.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2015;29(12):2399-404. Retrospective multicentre study, 44 patients (26 men), mean follow-up 32.2 months; abstract states treatments with different combination or sequential modalities were used with variable results, that phototherapy (UVA1 or PUVA) was the treatment associated with higher although partial response, and concludes scleredema is a chronic debilitating disease unresponsive to various treatments but not necessarily a life-threatening condition. Contains no pulmonary function or imaging data.

sourceReferences.citation: Ibrahim RA, Abdalla NEH, Shabaan EAH, et al. An Unusual Presentation of a Rare Scleroderma Mimic: What is Behind the Scenes? Curr Rheumatol Rev. 2019;15(2):172-175. doi: 10.2174/1573397114666180808091621. PMID 30088450.
sourceReferences.note: Case of scleredema presenting as a rare scleroderma mimic with diffuse skin thickening sparing the hands and feet, associated arthralgia, dysphagia, and dyspnoea on exertion, a restrictive pattern on pulmonary function testing, and interstitial lung fibrosis on high-resolution computed tomography, diagnosed on biopsy as scleredema in a patient subsequently found to have immunoglobulin A kappa multiple myeloma; registered as countervailing evidence with its myeloma and systemic-sclerosis confounding disclosed.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: Curr Rheumatol Rev. 2019;15(3):172-175. Case report; abstract states the patient did not fulfil ACR/EULAR systemic sclerosis criteria, had no Raynaud's phenomenon, negative systemic sclerosis autoantibodies, and normal nail fold capillaroscopy, that pulmonary function tests showed a restrictive pattern and high-resolution CT showed interstitial lung fibrosis, and that serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation, and bone marrow biopsy led to a diagnosis of scleredema associated with immunoglobulin A kappa multiple myeloma.

governanceNotes: D1 batch 81 (2026-09-27): three bounded association edges added - scleredema to diabetes-mellitus (rank 1, MULTIFACTORIAL), scleredema to multiple-myeloma (rank 2, MULTIFACTORIAL), and scleredema to interstitial-lung-disease (rank 3, MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE), all classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The primary shared anchor is the 44-patient multicentre series reporting 30 patients with diabetes mostly type 2, 5 confirmed monoclonal gammopathies, 2 deaths from cardiovascular complications due to myeloma and severe diabetes, phototherapy as the treatment with higher partial response, and an express NULL for preceding respiratory tract infection (PMID 26304054). Supporting anchors are the prospective screening of 113 diabetes patients identifying 11 new cases at 9.7 percent, all type 2 (PMID 33952255); the paraprotein-associated case report treated with intravenous immunoglobulin and narrow-band phototherapy (PMID 34858014); the monoclonal gammopathy of unknown significance progression case (PMID 37701163); the scleredema diabeticorum cuirasse-pattern case with restrictive lung disease and the explicit cutaneous-hardness mobility statement (PMID 33865279); and the scleroderma-mimic case with interstitial lung fibrosis registered as countervailing rather than supporting evidence (PMID 30088450). Two material disclosures travel on the face of these edges: the scleroderma route is withheld as DIFFERENTIAL because the located evidence reports non-criteria for systemic sclerosis rather than co-occurrence, and the pulmonary route discloses a parenchymal-versus-mechanical target-identity mismatch.
